argument_summary: The certification defense should be read narrowly, not as a claim of clean compliance. The admissible record supports the direction of certification because the current release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.2 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while public governance guidance supports proceeding with explicit documentation of current limitations and risk-management measures. The same admissible record also limits the claim: the fraud dispute review slice is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold, prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and eval batch, and the manual-monitoring comment is not an approved mitigation. On that record, the supportable position is that certification is defensible only on a constrained basis if the packet itself squarely treats the fraud slice weakness as a current limitation that must be disclosed under policy, rather than treating prior approval or informal monitoring as substitutes.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required to distinguish this case from clean compliance. The remaining gap can be handled by keeping the certification support bounded and by avoiding any overclaim that the current-release predicate has already been fully satisfied by stale approval or informal monitoring. That approach preserves governance accuracy without converting a supportable but limited certification rationale into a broader escalation claim.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit treating prior approval or informal monitoring as governance substitutes for the current release. It does permit a narrower certification position when the packet accurately reflects current evaluation results and carries forward the material segment weakness as a required disclosure item unless approved mitigation exists. The actor is therefore not defending unconditional compliance; the defendable policy claim is limited, caveated support tied to explicit acknowledgment of the current fraud dispute review weakness.
concessions: The admissible record does not show that current release documentation already reflects the fraud dispute review regression.
The admissible record does not include an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for the current subgroup weakness.
Prior approval is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
Informal manual monitoring cannot be presented as satisfying the policy requirement.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is added. No private context is offered as public support.
